question: How can application configuration be updated in Kubernetes without rebuilding the container image?

ground_truth.answer: Store configuration in a ConfigMap and inject it into containers in two ways. First, via the envFrom field of Container using an EnvFromSource with a configMapRef: all keys become environment variables, but the change only takes effect after a Pod restart. Second, via a volume: a ConfigMapVolumeSource is listed in the Pod volumes array and a VolumeMount inside the container maps a filesystem path to that volume. When mounted as a volume, Kubernetes propagates ConfigMap updates to the mounted files without a Pod restart, though the application must re-read the files to pick up the changes.
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.ConfigMap: stores non-sensitive configuration data as key-value pairs accessible to Pods
io.k8s.api.core.v1.EnvFromSource: injects all keys from a ConfigMap or Secret as environment variables into a container
io.k8s.api.core.v1.ConfigMapVolumeSource: projects a ConfigMap into a volume so its keys appear as files in the container filesystem
io.k8s.api.core.v1.VolumeMount: specifies the path inside a container at which a volume is mounted
